name: Composite Hemangioendothelioma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Immunohistochemical Diagnostic Criteria for Composite Hemangioendothelioma

criteria.description: Presence of a vascular tumor with a mixture of benign, intermediate, and malignant endothelial components on histology
Positive endothelial markers including CD31, CD34, and ERG on immunohistochemical staining
Cutaneous or subcutaneous mass typically located on distal extremities or trunk

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of mixed vascular tumor components with positive endothelial markers is required; clinical presentation supports diagnosis.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on histopathological and immunohistochemical evaluation due to overlapping features with other vascular tumors.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multifocal cutaneous or subcutaneous vascular nodules
pathognomonic.notes: Typically presents as multiple nodules or plaques on skin or subcutaneous tissue.
searchTerms: multiple skin or under-skin blood vessel lumps
clusters of blood vessel bumps under skin

pathognomonic.notes: Lesions often have a purple discoloration due to vascular nature.
searchTerms: purple discoloration on skin that grows slowly

common.symptomName: Local tenderness or discomfort at lesion site
common.notes: Mild pain or tenderness may be reported.
searchTerms: pain or soreness at skin lump

common.notes: Ulceration can occur in advanced or larger lesions.
Lesions typically grow over months to years.
searchTerms: gradual increase in skin mass size

common.notes: Enlarged lymph nodes may be palpable near lesion.

occasional.notes: Swelling may be due to tumor mass effect.
searchTerms: painful swelling in arm or leg

occasional.symptomName: Limited range of motion near lesion site
occasional.notes: Mass effect may restrict joint movement.

occasional.symptomName: Mild systemic symptoms such as low-grade fever
occasional.notes: Rarely, mild constitutional symptoms may be present.
searchTerms: slight systemic symptoms like mild fever

rare.symptomName: Distant metastases to lung or bone
rare.notes: Metastasis is rare but possible in aggressive cases.
searchTerms: cancer spread to lungs or bones
tumor metastasis in chest or skeleton
distant tumor growth in lung or bone

rare.notes: Secondary lymphedema due to lymphatic obstruction.
searchTerms: swelling due to lymph fluid buildup

laboratory: No specific laboratory abnormalities; routine blood tests usually normal
imaging: MRI or ultrasound showing heterogeneous vascular masses with mixed solid and cystic components
CT scan may be used to assess for deep tissue involvement or metastasis
genetic: No consistent genetic mutations identified; some cases show complex karyotypes
other: Histopathology reveals a mixture of benign, intermediate, and malignant vascular endothelial components
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD31, CD34, ERG endothelial markers

distinguishingFeatures: Histology shows spindle cell proliferation with slit-like vascular spaces
Typically shows epithelioid endothelial cells with myxohyaline stroma
High-grade malignant vascular tumor with marked cellular atypia
Histology shows irregular anastomosing vascular channels with pleomorphic endothelial cells

redFlags: Evidence of regional lymphadenopathy or distant metastasis
references: Fetsch JF, et al. Composite hemangioendothelioma: a clinicopathologic study of 17 cases. Am J Surg Pathol. 2000.
Requena L, et al. Vascular tumors of the skin: an update. Semin Diagn Pathol. 2017.
